controlLens.name: NIST SP 800-53 Revision 5
controlLens.scopeNote: Architecture planning aid only. These mappings identify cloud decisions that can support control implementation and evidence planning; they do not determine applicability, implementation sufficiency, assessment results, or authorization.

families.name: Access Control
families.applicability: Shape application and administrative access boundaries, privileged paths, network-restricted service access, and policy enforcement points.
reviewPrompts: Where is authorization enforced for users, workloads, and administrators?
Which public or private paths must be denied by default and evidenced?

families.name: Audit and Accountability
families.applicability: Plan traceable audit events, centralized collection, retention, review, and evidentiary access protection.
reviewPrompts: Which application and platform events must be captured and retained?
Who can alter, query, export, or delete audit evidence?

families.name: Assessment, Authorization, and Monitoring
families.applicability: Organize continuous posture review, regulated-hosting evidence, findings workflow, and authorization boundary decisions.
reviewPrompts: What boundary and authorization assumptions need evidence?
Which findings and changes trigger reassessment?

families.name: Configuration Management
families.applicability: Treat infrastructure definitions, policies, baselines, approvals, drift findings, and changes as controlled artifacts.
capabilities: Infrastructure as Code & Policy as Code
reviewPrompts: How are Terraform and native policy changes reviewed, approved, deployed, and recovered?
How is drift identified against approved application and platform baselines?

families.name: Contingency Planning
families.applicability: Relate workload recovery objectives to backups, restore validation, regional recovery, migration rollback, and dependencies.
reviewPrompts: Which application recovery objectives are tested rather than assumed?
How are recovery dependencies and restoration evidence protected?

families.name: Identification and Authentication
families.applicability: Design workforce, workload, service, and privileged identities together with key, secret, and certificate handling.
reviewPrompts: How are human and workload identities issued, authenticated, rotated, and revoked?
Where are application secrets and cryptographic identities stored and audited?

families.name: Risk Assessment
families.applicability: Expose risks from public attack surface, vulnerable configuration, regulated data location, AI usage, and provider capability constraints.
reviewPrompts: Which threats, data flows, and provider limitations materially affect the application?
How are findings tracked through design and operational review?

families.name: System and Services Acquisition
families.applicability: Make cloud-service selection, platform standards, secure delivery, and infrastructure automation deliberate acquisition and engineering decisions.
capabilities: Infrastructure as Code & Policy as Code
reviewPrompts: Which service and tooling requirements must be imposed before application delivery?
What supply-chain and lifecycle evidence is required from pipelines and modules?

families.name: System and Communications Protection
families.applicability: Plan segmentation, private access, encryption, key control, edge exposure, and trustworthy communications paths.
reviewPrompts: Where do trust boundaries, ingress, egress, and cryptographic protections exist?
Which managed-service endpoints require private or inspected connectivity?

families.name: System and Information Integrity
families.applicability: Connect vulnerability and configuration findings with telemetry, incident visibility, and application integrity decisions.
reviewPrompts: How are flaws, anomalous behavior, and integrity findings detected and acted on?
Which application signals and cloud findings are correlated for response?

families.name: Supply Chain Risk Management
families.applicability: Govern infrastructure modules, pipeline dependencies, artifact provenance, approved components, and deployment paths.
capabilities: Infrastructure as Code & Policy as Code
reviewPrompts: How are Terraform modules, providers, actions, images, and dependencies approved and pinned?
What evidence connects a reviewed change to the deployed application environment?

patterns.name: Secure Internet-Facing Application Foundation
patterns.summary: A starting control plane and service path for public web applications that need protected ingress, private service access, operational evidence, and recovery planning.
patterns.whenToUse: Use for customer or partner applications exposed through public endpoints, before selecting application runtime or delivery implementation details.
reviewPrompts: Where is the public trust boundary and how is the origin protected?
Which identity, logging, security-finding, and recovery controls are platform owned?
Do regulated data paths require product-by-product availability confirmation?
patterns.verificationNote: This is a planning overlay inferred from provider framework and landing-zone guidance. Validate workload threat model, data classification, regions, and regulated-service support before design approval.

patterns.name: Regulated Workload Control Boundary
patterns.summary: A control-focused starting point for workloads whose architecture review must explicitly address identity, encryption, network boundaries, monitoring, security findings, recovery, and sovereign or regulated hosting options.
patterns.whenToUse: Use while scoping a workload that may handle regulated information or operate under government or sovereign-cloud requirements.
capabilities: Infrastructure as Code & Policy as Code
reviewPrompts: Which control regime, boundary, and evidence requirements actually apply?
Which mapped service features are confirmed in the selected regulated environment?
What recovery, cryptography, identity, and logging evidence must be retained?
patterns.verificationNote: This pattern identifies review areas; it is not a compliance determination or authorization claim. Unknown regulated availability and parity values require direct provider confirmation.

patterns.name: Data & Generative AI Platform Foundation
patterns.summary: A governed base for enterprise analytics and generative AI initiatives, connecting data storage and analysis with models, retrieval, agents, accelerator capacity, identity, cryptography, private access, monitoring, and FinOps.
patterns.whenToUse: Use when evaluating internal analytics, retrieval-augmented generation, agentic workflows, model training, self-hosted inference, or governed AI product platforms.
reviewPrompts: What data is allowed into model prompts, training, retrieval, agent memory, tool calls, and analytics paths?
Which identity, tool authorization, encryption, private-access, evaluation, and cost controls are mandatory?
Are selected models and AI features available in the required region or regulated boundary?
patterns.verificationNote: Model catalogs and AI service support can change quickly. Recheck provider documentation, data-handling commitments, regional support, and regulated constraints during architecture review.

patterns.name: Hybrid Migration & Recovery Landing Path
patterns.summary: A structured starting path for moving existing estates into cloud while maintaining connectivity, identity, recovery, operational visibility, and cost governance.
patterns.whenToUse: Use during discovery and landing-zone planning for data center migration, hybrid extension, application transition, or staged modernization.
reviewPrompts: What dependencies, recovery objectives, data classifications, and cutover constraints exist?
Which network, identity, monitoring, and rollback capabilities must exist before migration waves begin?
How will post-migration ownership, optimization, and modernization decisions be governed?
patterns.verificationNote: Migration tooling maps differ across servers, storage, databases, and applications. Confirm target services, transfer paths, rollback design, and regulated-environment support per workload wave.
